mathematical_result.coprime_case: If gcd(m,A)=1, every packet word is primitive, N_orb=binom(A-1,m-1)/m, and N_pt=binom(A-1,m-1).
boundary_cases: m=1,A=1 gives the negative fixed point -1
m=1,A>=2 gives one positive rational fixed point
A=m>1 contains only the imprimitive all-ones word and contributes no exact-period-m orbit

proof_structure: Unique primitive-root decomposition partitions positive compositions by repetition number d dividing gcd(m,A).
Möbius inversion gives the primitive pointed-word count.
The cyclic action on a primitive word is free, so division by m gives necklaces.
MOR-COL-000064 transports necklaces exactly to rational odd-return orbits; MOR-COL-000065 fixes the exact-period interpretation across clocks.
CLM-COL-000183 gives each rotated point as a positive numerator divided by 2^A-3^m, so one packet has a uniform sign.
The binomial identity converts the exponent-composition form into Stanley's fixed-content binary-necklace coefficient.
